function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|----------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often form channels, carriers, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (carrier)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors** (e.g., β‑adrenergic receptor, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor)
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases** (e.g., EGFR, HER2)
• **Ion channels** (e.g., voltage‑gated K⁺ channel Kv1.2, calcium channel Cav1.2)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels)
• **Integrins** (cell‑matrix adhesion)
• **Cadherins** (cell‑cell adhesion) | | **Peripheral (non‑integral) proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via lipid anchors or interactions with integral proteins. | • **Ankyrin‑R** (links integral proteins to the cytoskeleton)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane stability)
• **Band‑3 protein** (anion exchanger, peripheral to the membrane)
• **Glycophorin A** (glycoprotein on erythrocyte surface, peripheral) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to lipids (e.g., GPI anchors) and reside on the outer leaflet. | • **CD59** (protectin, GPI‑anchored)
• **CD55 (decay‑accelerating factor)** (GPI‑anchored)
• **Prion protein (PrP^C)** (GPI‑anchored) | | **Extracellular matrix‑binding proteins** | Interact with the extracellular matrix or other cells. | • **Fibronectin** (extracellular matrix protein that binds integrins)
• **Collagen type IV** (basement membrane component) | ### How to use this list - **Research**: If you’re studying a particular cell type, look up which of these proteins are expressed in that tissue (e.g., neurons have many ion channels and neurotransmitter receptors). - **Drug targeting**: Many drugs target plasma‑membrane receptors (GPCRs, RTKs) or ion channels. - **Diagnostics**: Surface markers (e.g., CD antigens) are used in flow cytometry to identify cell populations. Feel free to ask for more details on any specific protein family or for a curated list for a particular cell type!
